comment: Ballistic Dynamics projectiles. Units are in the field names; every number has a provenance note (docs/data-format.md). Stepped G1 coefficients apply at and above their _min_fps.

projectiles.name: .308 175 gr Sierra MatchKing (#2275)
projectiles.construction: hollow point boat tail, copper jacket over a lead core

provenance.diameter_in: published: Sierra Bullets catalogue, #2275 .30 cal 175 gr HPBT MatchKing
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 1.24 in as handloaders measure it; Sierra's catalogue page does not list it. To be replaced by a measurement before Milestone 3 uses it for stability
provenance.bc_g1: published: Sierra Bullets catalogue, #2275: .505 at 2800 fps and above, .496 from 1800 to 2800 fps, .485 below 1800 fps
provenance.bc_g1_min_fps: published: Sierra Bullets catalogue, #2275 velocity bands
provenance.bc_g7: published: B. Litz, Applied Ballistics for Long Range Shooting, measured G7 BC of the 175 gr SMK, 0.243 (Federal's GM308M2 page lists 0.25)

projectiles.name: 6.5 mm 140 gr Hornady ELD Match
projectiles.construction: polymer tip, boat tail, copper jacket over a lead core

provenance.diameter_in: published: Hornady catalogue, 6.5 mm (.264) 140 gr ELD Match
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 1.40 in, typical of 140 gr 6.5 mm VLD-class bullets; not used before Milestone 3
provenance.bc_g1: published: Hornady, 81500 load data as listed by retailers, G1 0.646 (Hornady's current page lists 0.610 from its Doppler re-measurement; see docs/validation.md)
provenance.bc_g7: published: Hornady, 81500 load data as listed by retailers, G7 0.326

projectiles.name: .338 250 gr Lapua Scenar
projectiles.construction: hollow point boat tail, copper jacket over a lead core

provenance.length_in: estimated: about 1.63 in for a 250 gr .338 match hollow point; not used before Milestone 3
provenance.bc_g7: published: Applied Ballistics (Litz), Lapua 250 Scenar G7 0.320

projectiles.name: .50 750 gr Hornady A-MAX
projectiles.construction: polymer tip, boat tail, copper jacket over a lead core

provenance.length_in: estimated: about 2.3 in for a 750 gr .50 match bullet; not used before Milestone 3
provenance.bc_g1: published: Hornady catalogue, G1 1.050 (Graf & Sons listing)

projectiles.name: 5.56 mm 62 gr M855 / SS109 (steel penetrator)
projectiles.construction: full metal jacket boat tail, steel tip penetrator over a lead core

provenance.diameter_in: published: 5.56x45 mm NATO bullet diameter, 0.224 in
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 0.91 in as commonly measured for M855; not used before Milestone 3
provenance.bc_g1: published: Federal XM855 load data, G1 0.304

projectiles.name: 9 mm 124 gr Speer Gold Dot hollow point

provenance.diameter_in: published: Speer reloading data, 9 mm Luger .355 in
provenance.mass_gr: published: Speer reloading data, 124 gr GDHP
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 0.6 in for a 124 gr 9 mm hollow point; not used before Milestone 3
provenance.bc_g1: published: Speer reloading data, 9 mm Luger 124 gr GDHP, G1 0.134

provenance.length_in: estimated: about 2.0 in; not published. A solid is longer than a lead-core bullet of the same weight, and Miller's rule (fitted to lead cores) then under-states its stability
provenance.bc_g1: published: CheyTac product page, G1 0.949 (average over 3,500 yd); Jamison quoted 0.940 (2009) and Doppler figures near 0.934 have been disputed

projectiles.name: 6.5 mm 147 gr Hornady ELD Match
projectiles.construction: polymer tip, boat tail, copper jacket over a lead core

provenance.diameter_in: published: Hornady catalogue, 6.5 mm (.264) 147 gr ELD Match
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 1.45 in for a 147 gr 6.5 mm VLD-class bullet
provenance.bc_g1: published: Hornady 81501 data as listed by GAP Precision, G1 0.697
provenance.bc_g7: published: Hornady 81501 data as listed by GAP Precision, G7 0.351

projectiles.name: 7.62×54R Type L light ball (M1908)
projectiles.construction: flat-base spitzer, steel or cupronickel-clad jacket over a lead core

provenance.mass_gr: published: Type L light ball 9.6 g (148 gr)
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 1.26 in (32 mm) for the L spitzer
provenance.bc_g1: published: (secondary) Wikipedia, 7.62×54mmR article (via search summaries; the figure is marked 'citation needed' there), L bullet G1 about 0.338
provenance.bc_g7: published: (secondary) Wikipedia, 7.62×54mmR article (via search summaries; the figure is marked 'citation needed' there), L bullet G7 about 0.185

projectiles.name: 7.62×54R 7N1 sniper (9.8 g, steel core)
projectiles.construction: boat tail, steel-clad jacket, steel core with an air pocket in the nose and a lead base

provenance.length_in: estimated: about 1.30 in (33 mm) for the 7N1 boat tail
provenance.bc_g1: published: (secondary) Wikipedia, 7.62×54mmR article (via search summaries; the figure is marked 'citation needed' there), 7N1 G1 about 0.411
provenance.bc_g7: published: (secondary) Wikipedia, 7.62×54mmR article (via search summaries; the figure is marked 'citation needed' there), 7N1 G7 about 0.206

projectiles.name: 9 mm 115 gr full metal jacket (Federal American Eagle)
projectiles.construction: round-nose full metal jacket over a lead core

provenance.diameter_in: published: SAAMI 9 mm Luger bullet diameter 0.355 in
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 0.57 in, typical of 115 gr 9 mm round-nose FMJ
provenance.bc_g1: published: Federal AE9DP ballistic chart, BC 0.12

projectiles.name: 9 mm 124 gr full metal jacket (NATO-weight ball)
projectiles.construction: round-nose full metal jacket over a lead core

provenance.diameter_in: published: SAAMI 9 mm Luger bullet diameter 0.355 in
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 0.61 in, typical of 124 gr 9 mm round-nose FMJ (the NATO ball weight)
provenance.bc_g1: published: Federal AE9AP ballistic chart, BC 0.15

projectiles.name: .45 ACP 230 gr full metal jacket round nose
projectiles.construction: round-nose full metal jacket over a lead core

provenance.diameter_in: published: SAAMI .45 Auto bullet diameter 0.452 in
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 0.68 in, typical of the 230 gr .45 ball round nose
provenance.bc_g1: published: Federal AE45A ballistic chart, BC 0.19 (a retailer's table gives G1 0.193)

projectiles.name: .357 158 gr jacketed soft point
projectiles.construction: flat-nose jacketed soft point, lead core

provenance.diameter_in: published: SAAMI .357 Magnum bullet diameter 0.357 in
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 0.69 in for a 158 gr .357 flat-nose JSP
provenance.bc_g1: published: Federal AE357A ballistic chart, BC 0.2 (Magtech's 158 gr SJSP lists 0.172)

projectiles.name: 5.7 mm 40 gr V-MAX (FN SS197SR)
projectiles.construction: polymer tip, boat tail, copper jacket over a lead core

provenance.diameter_in: published: 5.7x28 mm bullet diameter 5.70 mm (0.224 in)
provenance.mass_gr: published: FN SS197SR, 40 gr Hornady V-MAX
provenance.length_in: estimated: about 0.68 in, as Hornady's 40 gr .224 V-MAX
provenance.bc_g1: estimated: Hornady's published G1 0.200 for its 40 gr .224 V-MAX (#22241); FN does not publish a BC for SS197SR, whose bullet may differ in shape
